title: Spark fails at dropDuplicates() due to multiple ExecutorLostFailure
question:
I have 479 parquet files (each approx. 120 MB, totaling a little over 2 billion records) stored on HDFS and I was trying to determine the best Spark configuration for this dataset, but I am unable to complete the dropDuplicates() operation. My HDFS configuration is:

NameNode: 4 core/24 GB RAM; 3 DataNode: 8 core/24 GB RAM

The PySpark code I tried to execute is:

from pyspark.conf import SparkConf
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

configuration = {
    "spark.sql.debug.maxToStringFields": 100,
    "spark.executor.cores": 7,
    "spark.executor.memory": "21g",
    "spark.executor.instances": 3,
}
config = SparkConf().setAll(configuration.items())
spark = (
    SparkSession.builder.master("spark://192.168.1.1:7077")
    .config(conf=config)
    .appName("my_app")
    .getOrCreate()
)
df = spark.read.parquet(f"{directory}/*.parquet").dropDuplicates()
df.count()

answer:
Consider doing df.agg(f.countDistinct("primary_key1", "primary_key2", ... "primary_keyn")).show()

df.dropDuplicates("primary_key1", "primary_key2", ... "primary_keyn").count().show() is an un-optimised way to achieve the same.

If you don't know the primary columns, consider doing a df.agg(f.countDistinct("*")).show()

My best guess to what is happening is that there are too many keys (hashes) to be created. Behind the scene, spark is trying to create hash of the column values combinations. That is how it does a dropDuplicates()
